newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Mark recovers as Kohl talks tough on euro.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Mark recovers as Kohl talks tough on euro.

text.p: The dollar's early surge on fears about the single European currency diminished on Wednesday after German leader Helmut Kohl pledged Bonn remained on track for monetary union despite a bruising row with the Bundesbank.
Worries about Bonn's failure to carry the day in its row with the central bank over revaluing reserves prompted the dollar to zip nearly a pfennig higher to a four-week high in early trade.
But a series of statements by Kohl, Finance Minister Theo Waigel and Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer calmed the wobbly foreign exchange market and the mark recovered a bit.

The row appeared to have little impact on German shares, which put on moderate gains along with Europe's other big bourses. But government bond markets were unsettled over concerns about events in Germany and interest rate worries in Britain.

Chancellor Kohl threw his weight fully behind Waigel in parliament after his embattled ally lost his grab for Bundesbank gold to help Germany qualify for the euro by filling a gap in government finances.
Kohl told a stormy parliament session that Waigel would stay in office and Germany would still meet the strict Maastricht criteria for the launch of monetary union (EMU) in 1999.

"A delay would have an enormous impact on financial markets and the German economy's chances in the export market," Kohl said. "The German government will keep firmly to the timetable and criteria for currency union."

Under a Bonn-Bundesbank compromise, funds from the asset revaluation will now be transferred to the government in 1998 instead of this year, which the market saw as increasing the chances that a broad group of countries would launch EMU.

"The mark is in all sorts of problems in Europe because of the gold row and although the heat has come off that problem, the general story the market is fixed on is on a soft euro," said David Brown, chief European economist at Bear Stearns in London.
"The market view is that anything that heralds a softer euro is good for the dollar."
The dollar was nearly a pfennig higher at one point, but by 1130 GMT it was quoted at 1.7309 marks and 116.33 yen, compared with 1.7263 marks and 116.06 yen in late European trading on Tuesday.
Europe's major stock markets all showed gains, with Paris clawing its way back from opening losses as the market waited for new Prime Minister Lionel Jospin to name his government.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index was off its highs but still showing a rise of 14.58 points, or 0.56 percent, at 2,639.07 at mid-session as the market continued to recover following the Socialist election victory on Sunday.
Dealers said the market was supported by dollar firmness, rises on other stockmarkets and expectations of a moderate Socialist government.
Hotel group Accor gave back its early rise, falling 0.71 percent to 843 francs after it forecast 25 percent higher profit from the budget sector this year.
Leading British shares snapped a five-day losing streak with a small bounce, getting early support from a firm close on Wall Street where the Dow ended up 22 points.
By mid-session, the benchmark FTSE 100 was up 24.7 points at 4,582.5 amid renewed strength in bank shares and a buoyant futures market.
British shares hesitated briefly after news the Purchasing Mangers Index rose for the 11th consecutive month in May, which dealers said reinforced the view that interest rates are poised to rise.

"The numbers look strong and I think it's fair to say that they reflect a threat of inflation," said one dealer. "But we've been talking about higher rates for some time now and I think the 2.5 percent correction we had in the last week factors in a quarter point rate increase."
In Frankfurt, Germany's 30-share DAX index played catch up in early bourse trade to match gains in electronic screen trade late on Tuesday.
By 1130 GMT the DAX was showing gains of 35 points, or nearly one percent, with the dollar, debt market and Wall Street's overnight close underpinning sentiment.
The soothing words from both sides on the Bundesbank-Bonn gold revaluation row were seen as mostly market neutral.
CURRENCIES AT1130 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7309 marks and 116.33 yen compared with 1.7263 marks and 116.06 yen in late European trading on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1130 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 24.7 points, or 0.54 percent, at 4,582.5.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 14.58 points, or 0.56 percent, at 2,639.07.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 35.76 points, or 0.99 percent, at 3,661.5.
PRECIOUS METALS

Gold was fixed easier at $342.55 versus $343.55 on Tuesday afternoon and a $342.85 close. Platinum was fixed at a new 16-month high of $425.00, while palladium fixed at highest-ever level of $210.00. Silver was up a cent at $4.75.
